name: @fossil-lang/corpus
description: Open a fossil/1 corpus and read it: fossil.json parsed once, a view per table on the host's DuckDB engine, and scan/sql over those views. Pure TypeScript — no WASM, no engine of its own; DuckDB prunes the Parquet row groups. fossil ships no viewer; @kanzo-tech/graph is the one there is.
//name: This was `@fossil-lang/graph` and it does not draw one. Its door is `open`, what comes back is a `Corpus`. The package that DOES put vertices on a GPU — `@kanzo-tech/graph` — is its one viewer. See /docs/design/corpus.
//exports: ONE entry. `.` is the door: `open` and `FOSSIL_FORMAT`, plus the manifest's and the scan's types. There is no WASM behind it any more — the reader was `fossil-graph` compiled to wasm32 and it is `JSON.parse` plus the SQL a scan composes — so importing it costs nothing a bundler has to emit.
//contract: `conformance/`, `guards/` and `integration/` are the corpus contract, and they live beside the reader that fulfils it. None of the three is in `files`, so npm never sees them. `guards/` stays plain ESM with no dependencies and no build — node plus the `duckdb` binary — because it is the directory a third party copies. **`test` is `vitest run` over `tests/` and nothing else**: `release.yml` runs `pnpm --filter "./packages/*" test` before publishing, on a runner with no `duckdb`, and a suite that spawned it in that step is what took `v0.3.0-alpha.4` down. The contract runs under its own names: `test:contract` is the guards' self-test, the checked-in corpus through the guards and its recipe; `test:integration` writes corpora with the `duckdb` binary and reads them back through `src/`, under its own vitest config.

scripts.test:contract: node guards/self-test.mjs && node guards/check.mjs conformance/corpus && node conformance/provenance.mjs
